criteria.label: Terrain similarity
criteria.description: Slope, roughness and trafficability relative to the reference terrain.
criteria.earth_proxy: SRTM / Copernicus DEM slope & roughness in AOI

criteria.label: Geological similarity
criteria.description: Lithology / process match (basaltic, impact, aqueous alteration, glacial...).
criteria.earth_proxy: USGS planetary analog resources + peer-reviewed literature

criteria.label: Illumination contrast
criteria.description: Polar night / low sun angle / long shadow proxy (Moon-weighted).

criteria.label: Ice / permafrost relevance
criteria.description: Presence of ground ice, permafrost or glacial ice as a process analog.

criteria.label: Subsurface / cave access
criteria.description: Accessible lava tubes, caves or skylights for subsurface robotics.

criteria.label: Operational testing suitability
criteria.description: Access, permits, logistics and safety for hardware/crew field tests.

objectives.label: General analog fidelity
objectives.description: Balanced weights from the body profile.

objectives.label: Rover mobility
objectives.description: Trafficability, slopes, dust and logistics for rover testing.

objectives.label: ISRU / resource prospecting
objectives.description: Ice and resource prospecting, extraction tests.

objectives.label: Habitat testing
objectives.description: Long-duration habitation, thermal stress and isolation logistics.

objectives.label: Cave exploration
objectives.description: Subsurface robotics in lava tubes and caves.

objectives.label: Astronaut field operations
objectives.description: EVA procedures, field geology training and crew logistics.

moon: Lunar gravity (1/6 g) — affects mobility, dust settling, drilling reaction forces and human locomotion.
Hard vacuum — no convective cooling, outgassing, cold welding and vacuum-specific lubrication behaviour.
Cryogenic permanently shadowed regions far colder than any Earth environment.
Unweathered, sharp, electrostatically charged regolith grains.
Space radiation (solar particle events, galactic cosmic rays) without a magnetosphere or atmosphere.
~29.5-Earth-day synodic day/night cycle and extreme thermal cycling.
mars: Thin CO2 atmosphere (~0.6 kPa mean surface pressure) — affects heat transfer, aerodynamics, dust lofting.
Surface radiation environment (no global magnetic field, thin atmosphere).
Planet-wide oxidising/perchlorate-bearing regolith chemistry at Martian scale.
Global dust storms and their duration.
Earth sites are biologically active; planetary-protection contamination conditions cannot be reproduced.
